title: Chapter 2: Walking the Beaten Path Together 6
content: But I thought it was worth the wait.
When Erika emerged from the shop, she looked like an adventurer.
To avoid any misunderstandings, adventurers tend to show quite a bit of skin. This is because they can use Body Enhancement magic.
Many of them don’t consider it rude to expose their skin, prioritizing ease of movement instead. If they can use sufficient Body Enhancement, defense isn’t an issue.
The outfit Erika chose, while still adhering to adventurer standards, was relatively modest.
She wore knee-high boots and a short cape, likely equipped with a magic tool for temperature regulation.
Though she was in pants, her thighs were boldly exposed, and her shoulders were bare.
By noble standards, it would be considered scandalous, but by adventurer standards, it fell within the realm of modesty.

Thanks to the development of magic tools, the price of clothing had dropped significantly, but it was clear from how well it fit Erika and showcased her figure that this was not just a mass-produced item. It was undoubtedly a type of magic tool in itself.
This adventurer gear, made from materials sourced from monsters and adjustable to a certain extent, was certainly not something a Rank 1 adventurer could afford.
But it suited Erika perfectly.
“How do I look?”
Erika asked.
C-c-c-cute…!
“You look strong.”
After a moment of hesitation, that was my answer.
“That's good to hear.”
[img]https://i.imgur.com/j4vK4al.jpeg

It seemed that saying she looked strong was the right response. I was glad I managed to hold back the urge to call her cute multiple times. Even now, I felt like shouting, “Erika is so cute!” if I let my guard down.
“And look here.”
She pointed to the arm area of her outfit.
What was it, I wondered, as I followed her fingertip to see a blue line running along the white fabric.
“Doesn’t it suit me?”
I nodded, slightly averting my gaze.
It seemed I was still shy about things I liked.
The weapon shop that Lana introduced me to was, to put it bluntly.
“It’s shabby.”
“It really is shabby.”
It was in terrible condition.
It was falling apart.

I couldn't believe they were trying to conduct business in such a state. If it hadn’t been for Lana’s introduction, I wouldn’t have even considered entering. In fact, I probably wouldn’t have even realized it was a weapon shop.
Erika looked at me with questioning eyes, as if asking what I would do, so I steeled myself and stepped forward.
Opening the door while nervously wondering if it would fall apart at the slightest touch, I was surprised to find the interior was unexpectedly clean.
Clean? More like…
“There’s nothing here.”
Erika said from behind me. There were no weapons, no shelves, nothing at all in the store.
For a moment, I thought I had entered the wrong shop, but there was a wooden sign on the counter that read “Tororosso Weapon Shop.”
Confused by the lack of displayed products and even the absence of people, I walked up to the counter.
There wasn’t even a bell to call for assistance, and as I looked down at the counter, I saw a person sprawled out.
“A corpse?”
“If you suspect that, you should be more surprised.”
For some reason, Erika looked exasperated.
“I’m sorry, I’m sorry.”
The woman, with messy black hair that reached her waist, shook her head vigorously while wearing glasses, and her apology was a bit frightening.
“I was so bored that I accidentally fell asleep, and I’m sorry for startling you.”
Even if she was bored, I wished she wouldn’t sleep in a place like this.
I panicked, thinking I might have stumbled upon a murder scene.
“Honestly, I didn’t feel any presence at all, so I thought it was a corpse.”
When Erika protested, the black-haired woman apologized again, shaking her hair.
“Well, that aside…”
Erika interrupted the apologizing woman and continued.
“Do you handle weapons here?”
She glanced at the counter.
“Tororosso, is it?”
“Oh, I’m sorry for the delay! I’m Tepe Tororosso, the owner of this weapon shop. Um, you’re a customer, right?”
That was a rather unusual way of speaking. Given her accent, she might be from the southern region.
“Yeah, I’m a customer. I came to buy a sword.”
“Whoa!”
Tepe let out an excited squeal at my response.
What should I do? I want to go home right now.
“Ah, I’m so sorry!”
It seemed my expression gave it away, as Tepe clung to my arm.
Caught off guard by her unexpected strength, I almost lost my balance for a moment.
“I got so excited because it’s been a while since I had a customer.”
Tepe looked at me with teary eyes.
“Alright, alright.”
I wanted her to let go quickly.
Erika’s expression had turned slightly displeased.

As a former marquis daughter, seeing a shopkeeper with such poor manners must have been unpleasant for her. But Tepe didn’t let go of my arm; instead, she started to stroke it, murmuring “Wow” and “Oh.”
Each time, her ample chest pressed against my arm.
Even through the rough leather apron, I couldn’t help but be aware of it.
Just as I was about to yell at her to let go, Tepe finally lifted her gaze from my arm.

“Customer, you’re quite rare. Your build suggests you’re a pure swordsman, and it seems you can use Body Enhancement magic with considerable strength… but you seem to struggle with release-type magic.”
She suddenly pinpointed my swordsmanship style.
Wait, was she looking at my muscles?
No, but can you really tell just from muscles?
It was true that my swordsmanship was a blend of knightly sword techniques learned at the academy and the southern-style swordsmanship taught by my master, which had shaped my current style.
“Oh, and you’re mostly a pure swordsman, right? It seems you can use Body Enhancement magic quite well, but… you seem to be quite poor at attack magic.”
It was frightening how she kept guessing my traits.
To be able to deduce that just from looking at my arm’s muscles was not normal.
A sense of fear began to well up within me.
“Stop there.”
Erika’s voice cut off whatever else Tepe was about to say.
“It’s excessive to talk about someone without their permission.”
At Erika’s cold tone, Tepe squeaked and released my arm, bowing her head in apology.

Since I felt she hadn’t meant any harm, I found her repeated apologies somewhat pitiful. Each time she apologized, her hair brushed against my face, so I tried to reassure her that I didn’t mind, but for some reason, I ended up getting scolded too.
“Where is there a husband who lets another woman cling to him in front of his wife?”
As I reflected on how I had failed to consider that while participating in this farce, I felt deep shame.
Tepe and I both apologized to Erika, and after somehow being forgiven, we exchanged nods.
For some reason, I felt a strange sense of camaraderie. Erika could be scary when she was angry.
Experiencing the same fear seemed to create a bond.
“Um… judging by your muscles, you seem to be a pure swordsman with excellent Body Enhancement capabilities, is that correct?”
After being admonished by Erika, Tepe confirmed with me.
Her assessment was accurate; I was extremely poor at magic.
To be precise, I could say I couldn’t use attack magic at all.
I didn’t know why, but I couldn’t draw magic power from within my body.
I could construct magic circles without issue, but the magic power generated wouldn’t leave my body, which was tantamount to being unable to use attack magic.
It wasn’t that I couldn’t produce any magic at all; I could use purification magic and create small sparks, which are considered lifestyle magic.
In exchange, I excelled at magic that didn’t require releasing magic power, like Body Enhancement, and I could boast about its strength.
Tepe nodded as I agreed.
“Then do you remember your skills?”
“I have a bit of Presence Detection, and according to my master, it seems I have swordsmanship-related skills activated.”
“Seems activated? You haven’t been appraised at the church?”
“I have my reasons.”
Skills.
If magic is a mimicry of divine works, then skills are gifts from the gods.
At least, that’s what the church claims.
Unlike magic, skills cannot be learned and memorized.
Most people are said to learn skills through practical experience.
Some skills are easily understood as soon as they are learned, while others require a clear self-awareness to use, and some can be used without even realizing they are being used.
While they are similar to magic in that they require magic power to use, they don’t require the construction of magic circles.
The amount of magic power needed varies, but the consumption is significantly less compared to magic.
Some skills can even surpass ordinary attack magic, leading some adventurers to research ways to intentionally learn skills day and night.
However, when appraised at the church, one can find out what skills they possess.
That skill appraisal itself is said to be a skill, but curiously, this skill only manifests in the clergy of the church.
This is likely one reason the church claims skills are gifts from the gods.
I felt I had learned my skills while working as an adventurer in the Faltarl Kingdom, but I didn’t feel any urgency to get them appraised, so I had never done so.
It wasn’t that I was reluctant to pay the appraisal fee or anything like that.
For that reason, I was unappraised regarding my skills, but now I found myself in a situation where I couldn’t easily go to the church.
At least, Erika couldn’t go; after all, from the church’s perspective, she was an attempted assassin of the Light Priestess.
It would be dangerous for her to even step onto church grounds.

As for me, I probably wouldn’t face the same level of danger, but it would be foolish to approach a precarious place voluntarily. From an adventurer’s standpoint, not knowing one’s skills is more than just foolish; it’s a matter of survival, but for now, I had no choice but to accept that.
So, we were both in a situation where we didn’t know our skills.
I merely shrugged at Tepe, who seemed to want to ask what my reasons were, indicating I had no intention of answering.
“I see, so you have your reasons. Well, that’s fine. Just from your muscles, I want to sell you a sword.”
Tepe’s peculiar phrasing made me tilt my head. It sounded as if she was choosing her customers.
When Tepe noticed my attitude, she clapped her hands.
“Did you come here without knowing about my shop?”
When I explained that I was referred by Lana from the Adventurer Guild, she nodded as if she understood.
“I’m sorry; that girl sometimes becomes a bit of a scatterbrain and probably forgot to explain.”
I didn’t have the image of her being scatterbrained, but I certainly had a strong impression of her being overly timid.
So, she’s scatterbrained on top of that.
“At my shop, I sell weapons based on my assessment of the person. Of course, I can also refuse if I see fit.”
“Is that how you do business?”
Erika asked, her genuine curiosity shining through.
Tepe smiled at her.
“Fortunately.”
Her face was filled with undeniable confidence.
I didn’t dislike that expression.
It was hard to believe she was the same person who had just said she was bored and had no customers.
“I believe you; you were able to deduce all that just from touching my arm.”
At my words, Tepe bowed her head as if we were old friends.
“Please wait a moment.”
Tepe announced before disappearing into the back of the shop, soon returning with a sword in hand.
It looked almost identical to the sword I had previously used.
There were hardly any decorations, and it gave off an intense sense of practicality, as if the creator had no interest in embellishments.
It felt different from mass-produced items that focused solely on practicality; there was a strong will behind it, perhaps because Tepe was the one who brought it.
I compared the sword to Tepe, who seemed to care nothing about her appearance, and thought about how a normal noble would react if I offered them this as their weapon.
They would likely get angry.
While nobles dislike decorations that compromise the functionality and essence of a weapon, most would be furious if presented with something so plain as their weapon.
But that wasn’t the case with this sword.
As I gripped the hilt placed on the counter, I was struck by the sword’s blade.
Made of iron and magic stone alloy, known as magic iron, the blade had a glossy sheen, and the balance when held was superb.
And then—
“I feel a sensation of magic power being absorbed. No, is it that the magic power is flowing through it?”
As I widened my eyes in surprise, Tepe nodded happily.
“Yes, that sword is designed to allow magic power to flow well through it. So—”
I understood what she was about to say before she finished.
I cast Body Enhancement on the sword before Tepe could complete her sentence.
Patterns resembling wood grain emerged on the sword’s surface.
“I wanted to explain that the sword also benefits from Body Enhancement, but…”
Tepe smiled wryly as I lightly apologized.
“I’m sorry for trying to surprise you; I’ve been using Body Enhancement on swords for a while now.”
“That’s quite a skillful thing to do.”
Tepe said with a hint of exasperation.
It seemed that using Body Enhancement on weapons was rare, even for a weapon shop owner.

“But this sword is amazing; it’s much easier to enhance than my previous sword, and it doesn’t feel like I’m forcing magic power through it at all. The quality of the enhancement is completely different.”
Tepe thanked me and bowed her head.
“I can confidently say it won’t break as long as it allows magic power to flow.”
As I returned the sword to the counter, I said.
“You’re overpraising me—oh, hehehe.”
Tepe began to squirm and wiggle her body.
If I was going to buy a sword, it would definitely be this one; I was certain of that as I glanced at Erika.
After all, she was the one holding the purse strings.
To be honest, I had enough financial support from the Prime Minister to not worry about living expenses, but according to Erika, managing the household finances was the wife’s role.
So, regarding Erika’s judgment.
Erika nodded.
“I’ll buy this sword.”
I said to Tepe.
The new sword, along with the plain scabbard I received as a bonus, looked so ordinary when hung at my waist that it could easily be mistaken for a common mass-produced sword.
Well, even when drawn, it would still look like just another mass-produced item unless closely examined.
As I listened to Tepe explain how to maintain the sword, its features, and what to do if it needed repairs, I was already satisfied with how it felt hanging at my waist.
“Well, basically, it’s just like a regular sword, so normal maintenance will be fine.”
“Thank you; I’ll make good use of it.”
When I expressed my gratitude, Tepe smiled and said she was glad to have made a sale.
By the way, it was quite a hefty sum.
Without Erika’s go-ahead, I might not have had the courage to buy it.
While I could earn a decent income as an adventurer, I tended to save money due to my frugal nature.
Speaking of which, I wondered what had happened to the money I saved in Faltarl?
I had informed my father about it, but he might have neglected to retrieve it from the Adventurer Guild, which he found troublesome.
“By the way, would you sell me a sword as well?”
As I pondered about the money I had left behind, Erika suddenly brought it up.
Since Erika already had a sword she brought from the Prime Minister’s household, she must have been genuinely interested in Tepe’s sword after seeing mine.
“May I see that sword?”
Tepe asked, and Erika silently offered her sword.
After examining the sword she drew from its scabbard for a moment, Tepe returned it to Erika, shaking her head.
“I’m sorry, but if you’re looking for a replacement for this sword, it would be faster to search the royal treasury.”
“I see. I was also interested in the shopkeeper’s sword, but that’s unfortunate.”
Erika said, genuinely disappointed as she returned the sword to her waist.
“While it’s not a replacement, please accept this.”
Tepe offered Erika a short dagger she had in its scabbard.
“The cost is on the house. It’s a thank you for allowing me to see the treasured sword of the Solnzali family up close.”
Tepe casually deduced that Erika was from the Solnzali family just by looking at the sword.
Who exactly is this person?
Erika accepted the dagger with a wry smile.
I couldn’t tell if it was in response to being recognized or something else.
“You’re quite good at business. I’ll leave the sword maintenance to you when it needs care.”
As I watched Tepe bow her head and Erika express her admiration for her upper-class demeanor, I felt a flutter of excitement when the door to the shop opened.
“Tepe! I brought what you asked for!”
A woman entered, carrying a large paper bag.
Upon hearing her voice, I felt a moment of apprehension, and then, seeing her outfit, my cheeks twitched slightly.
The woman, a sister, turned to face me and Erika and shouted.
“That adventurer from back then!”
The church, that is the group that claims to be the servants of God.
Their doctrine is simple: save the weak.
That’s really all there is to it. And they are faithful to that doctrine.
From top to bottom, you could say everyone is.
Of course, factions form within a group, but their factions arise from how to help the weak, so they are deeply committed.
They genuinely strive to save the weak, and there are churches all over the countries, with strong connections and immense support from the populace.

They are a group of magic experts who seek to master the divine works of God, far removed from worldly power, ranging from lowly priests and sisters to the upper echelons. From the perspective of the royal family and nobility, they are not exactly a favorable group, but their existence brings benefits.
They actively engage in saving the weak according to their doctrine, and from the viewpoint of the royal family and nobility, it’s welcome if they do it on their own.
The church’s disinterest in worldly power has also been convenient for them.
Thus, the church and the powerful have maintained a long-standing relationship of mutual respect while generally remaining uninvolved with each other.
However, when it comes to planning the assassination of the Light Priestess, that non-interference goes out the window.
I struggled to suppress the urge to click my tongue.
Hekatai is a large city.
As long as I didn’t approach the church, I wouldn’t encounter such situations; I cursed myself for having such a naive thought.
The sister approached us, flustered, clutching the large paper bag.
I would prefer to ignore her and leave the shop, but that seemed unlikely.
“You’re the Longdagger couple, right?”
The sister said, peering out from the bag.
I almost wanted to say she had the wrong person, but for some reason, Erika smiled and replied, “Yes, that’s right.”
The sister placed the bag on the counter and bowed her head.
“Thank you for what you did back then; thanks to you, both I and the village are safe.”
“No, we just completed the request.”
The sister smiled at my response.
I thought I had answered as curtly as possible, but was there something in my tone that made her smile?
“Yes, it was just a request from a girl.”
I inwardly clicked my tongue at the sister’s response. If she knew the circumstances, she would think of us as adventurers who fulfilled a girl’s request for free.
There was nothing beneficial for me in gaining favor with someone from the church.
In fact, I wished she would forget about it.
I racked my brain, trying to find a way to end the conversation and part ways, but a voice interrupted from the side.
“Shara, I hate to interrupt your excitement, but shouldn’t you introduce yourself?”
Well, I’m not excited at all.
Tepe said while checking the contents of the paper bag placed on the counter.
Her demeanor was quite casual, so they must be acquaintances or something. It felt like they were friends.
“Oh, I’m sorry. I’m Shara Lansura. As you can see, I’m a sister. Thank you very much for saving me and the village the other day.”
After quickly introducing herself and expressing her gratitude, Shara looked at us with sparkling eyes.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/ozOUdBE.jpeg
What is it? I wondered internally, only to receive an elbow jab from Erika standing next to me.
That’s when I realized.
“I’m Shin Longdagger, and this is my ‘wife,’ Erika Longdagger. As you can see, we’re adventurers, so that was just a job, so don’t worry about it.”

I had intended to avoid introducing myself entirely, but in my attempt to retreat, I had forgotten the basic courtesy of returning an introduction. To be honest, I didn’t want to say my name even now.
I could have given a fake name, but that might lead to trouble later.
